public_payload.normalized_proposition: Few people understand how chatbots work, and many anthropomorphize them, attributing real intelligence and emotion to them.

statement.excerpt: Few people understand how they work; many people anthropomorphizing those chatbots, attributing to them real intelligence and emotion.

from_speaker: Few people understand how they work
attributing to them real intelligence and emotion
our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns ordinary people and chatbot users, not only technical experts or selected enthusiasts.
Understanding means a basic functional understanding, not the ability to build a language model.
Anthropomorphism here includes literal attribution of intelligence and emotion; affection, politeness, or imaginative role play alone is insufficient.
Few and many express prevalence but supply no numerical cutoffs. No arbitrary percentage is imposed.
For this ongoing observation, use early 2023 through February 22 as the recent pre-publication period; no regular reporting interval is specified.
criteria.support_condition: Population evidence for the target period shows that basic understanding was uncommon and that literal attribution of intelligence and emotion to chatbots was widespread.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable population evidence shows that basic understanding was common or that the specified literal attributions were rare.

evidence.explanation: The study finds fragmented meanings in January 2023 Twitter discourse. That is relevant context, but it does not measure how many people understand chatbot operation or attribute real emotions to chatbots.

The survey collected responses in April and May 2023. It concerns mental capacities attributed to AI generally, so it cannot establish the prevalence of the specified chatbot beliefs before February 22.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Survey data collected before publication that directly test basic chatbot knowledge and distinguish literal belief in intelligence and emotions from attachment or role play, with sampling details and full question wording.
